title: CS Quest 4.1 · How a message travels (Packets, routes, protocols)
name: How a message travels (Packets, routes, protocols)
summary: Students act out how a message travels: a picture cut into numbered pieces is passed desk to desk by student routers and put back together by number. Then in Packet Post they help Pim break messages into packets in Break It Up and, when a road closes mid-send, reroute them in the first levels of Many Roads. Pairs share one device.
iCan: explain that a message is cut into small numbered pieces called packets
say that packets can take different roads and are put back together by their numbers
materials: Envelope Relay kit: one printed picture cut into 4 numbered pieces and 4 envelopes
doNow: How does a picture get from your tablet to a friend's tablet across town? Draw it in 3 boxes.
plan: Explore: Envelope Relay, then Break It Up level 1

warmup.why: first lesson of the unit: the unit opener, the vocabulary item and today's three exit items as a pre-test; nobody is expected to know them yet, so say so before you start

do: Run the Envelope Relay. Put the 4 numbered picture pieces in 4 envelopes. Pick four routers: students at four desks. Hand each envelope to a different router; each router passes it to another desk and on to the receiver at the front, who puts the picture back together by number.

Round 2: take envelope 3 out of the relay and hold it. Let the receiver find the gap, then send it again through a different desk. Then open Packet Post at Break It Up on the projector (Open game at this chapter) and play level 1 with the class.
say: The internet cuts everything into small pieces called packets. Each packet can take a different road through many computers and cables.
The numbers on the packets let the other end put the message back together, even when they arrive out of order.
ask: The pieces arrived 3, 1, 4, 2. How did our receiver know the right order?
explore.afterAsk: Take answers until someone says the numbers. Write on the board: a packet is a small numbered piece of a message. Then let Pim send the first message on the projector.
explore.bigIdea: Messages travel in numbered packets and get put back together at the other end.

play.goal: Break It Up, then 2 levels of Many Roads
play.pairs: driver and navigator on one device; swap at the chime every 2 levels; the navigator reads the packet numbers out loud before the driver sends
lookFors: trying to send the whole picture as one big packet
putting packets back in the order they arrived instead of by number
in Many Roads, waiting for the closed road to open instead of choosing another road
play.misconception: Packets do not have to take the same road or arrive in order: the numbers put them back together, and a closed road just means another road.
earlyFinishers: help a neighbor without touching their screen

discuss: What happened when the road closed? Did the message still arrive?
Why does every packet need a number?
showMe: One pair shows a Many Roads level on the projector; the class calls out the new road when the old one closes.

exit.sentencePrompt: What is a packet, and how does a message get put back together at the other end?
exit.frame: A packet is ___, and the message is put back together by ___.

rubric.line: Packets: how a message travels and is put back together
levels: Says a message is cut into pieces
Says the pieces (packets) travel separately and are put back together
Also says the numbers fix the order, or that packets can take another road

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: 3-packet levels with a glowing best road
the navigator lays the Envelope Relay pieces on the desk as a model
stretch: 3 stars on every level: the fewest hops

unpluggedTwin.title: Envelope Relay
materials: one printed picture cut into 4 to 6 numbered pieces
four to six student routers at their desks
steps: Put each numbered piece in an envelope. The sender at the back hands the envelopes to different routers.
Each router passes its envelope to another router of their choice, and the last one hands it to the receiver at the front.
The receiver opens the envelopes in the order they arrive and puts the picture back together by number.
Round 2: close a road: one router puts their head down and cannot pass anything. The others find another way.
Share: did the picture still arrive? What would have happened without the numbers?

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: how does a picture get from your tablet to a friend's tablet across town? Draw it in 3 boxes.

Play Packet Post, chapter Break It Up, in pairs for 20 minutes. Classes, then the lesson, then Play. If the game asks, the quest code is 1 1 0 0. Goal: Break It Up, then 2 levels of Many Roads. No warm-up and no projector needed; playing signed out is fine.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

shortPeriod40.discuss: What happened when the road closed? Did the message still arrive?
shortPeriod40.keep: the exit ticket is never cut

add: a longer Envelope Relay with 6 pieces and a closed road (15 minutes) before Play
10 minutes of the Unit 3 review on Brain Board as retrieval

notes: Say many computers and cables, not a one-word name for it; no real site names on the board (the game cannot show them either).
The warm-up is a pre-test for unit 4: nobody is expected to know the answers yet. Say so before you start.
The Explore is unplugged first: the Envelope Relay takes about 4 of the 6 minutes.
Shared devices: this is an odd lesson in the unit, so partner A signs in; the gradebook and the Standards tab count the signed-in student.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: How does a picture get from your tablet to a friend's tablet across town? Draw it in 3 boxes.

Big idea: Messages travel in numbered packets and get put back together at the other end.

We will talk about:
- What happened when the road closed? Did the message still arrive?
- Why does every packet need a number?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live. It is fine not to know them yet: we check again at the end.

steps.title: Play: Break It Up
steps.body:
Goal: Break It Up, then 2 levels of Many Roads. Stretch: Many Roads levels 3 and 4, then 3 stars. When Break It Up ends, the game takes you on to Many Roads.
If the game asks for a quest code, it is 1 1 0 0.
Pairs: driver and navigator. Swap when you hear the chime. The navigator reads the packet numbers out loud.
